subject: Operational Buoy: QBR pulse + targeted asks (May 19)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: leadership@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational Buoy: QBR pulse + targeted asks (May 19)

Good morning — sending a short pulse ahead of next week’s QBR. I’ve focused this note on wins we can call out, current risks that could land on the QBR table, and three immediate asks where I need quick direction.

Wins
- Performance: recent runtime changes reduced text-generation p99 CPU time for batch workloads by ~18% (15–30s sequences). We should include the p99 chart in the infra section.
- Sales/Dedicated: Two mid-market Dedicated deployments (Acme, Fathom Health) moved from staging to production this week — positive reference for the Dedicated roadmap.
- Optimize: Initial rollout of the new batching suggestion engine cut per-token cost for small-chat workloads by ~9% in our internal alpha.

Risks
- Capacity: eu-west GPU capacity is trending toward sustained saturation for the medium-seq LLM fleet next quarter; if not mitigated we’ll see higher tail latency for customers in the region.
- Billing spike: We observed an unexpected billing delta for a single large customer; procurement is reviewing but it could translate to a QBR ask on credits/adjustments.
- QBR prep: Slides are thin on cost-per-workload attribution — we need a concrete number for the exec deck.

Asks (short)
1) Approve provisional credit for Acme’s invoice while procurement completes the audit (recommendation: cap at $30k until we have final findings).
2) Approve short-term capacity relief for eu-west (burst contract with PartnerCloud for 4 weeks) while infra implements a model-routing mitigation. Estimated incremental spend: ~$18k/week.
3) Volunteer to own the Capacity slide in the QBR deck (data + action plan) — I can draft but need an owner to present.

Attachments: QBR_draft_v2.pptx (slides), p99_latency_dashboard.png (chart), acme_credit_request.pdf (invoice + request)

Next steps: If I don’t hear objections by EOD today I’ll greenlight the Acme provisional credit and open the PartnerCloud PO.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Note: Sam Holt at Acme was looped on the invoice thread earlier; I’ve summarized below for context (no action required from Sam for this internal decision).

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational Buoy: QBR pulse + targeted asks (May 19)

Jonas — thanks for the concise callout. Quick directions:
- Acme: Approve the provisional credit cap of $30k. Finance should proceed with a contingent credit memo and note that final will depend on procurement findings.
- Capacity: Approve the PartnerCloud burst while infra implements the routing mitigation, but limit to 3 weeks unless we see measurable tail improvements. Vanessa, please coordinate the PO.
- QBR slide owner: Karthik, can you take the Capacity slide and coordinate with Jonas on the data visuals?

I’ll review the deck by Thursday morning and flag anything that needs exec-level framing.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational Buoy: QBR pulse + targeted asks (May 19)

Thanks — I’ll take the Capacity slide. A few data asks from my side so the slide is actionable:
- Add cost-per-token by workload bucket (hosted API small-chat vs. long-seq generation) — needs to show delta pre/post batching suggestion rollout.
- Add a one-line mitigation timeline: immediate (PartnerCloud burst), 2–4 weeks (routing policy + autoscale tuning), 8–12 weeks (capacity expansion plan).

Also: recommend we include a quick note on graceful degradation policy (which model variants we fall back to) — that helps the execs tie capacity to customer impact. Jonas, can you share the dashboard slice for cost per workload? I’ll synthesize into one slide and coordinate with Mina for visuals.

Karthik
Director, Product Operations

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

- Processing provisional credit memo for Acme (cap $30k) — procurement/finance looped; I’ve attached acme_credit_request.pdf to the finance ticket.
- Opening PartnerCloud PO for 3 weeks of burst capacity (Vanessa, please proceed).
- Sharing cost-per-workload dashboard slice now: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/cost/workload?slice=qbr. Mina, I’d appreciate a quick visual treatment.
- Karthik: I’ll co-present the Capacity slide with you.

If anything else surfaces I’ll flag immediately; otherwise I’ll push the updated deck by Friday EOD.

Jonas
